ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=8$, $BC=4\sqrt{2}$, $DE\perp AC$ at point $F$, and intersects $AB$ at point $E$. Find the length of $DE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In rectangle $ABCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAB = \angle ADC = 90^\circ$, $CD = AB = 8$, $AD = BC = 4\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAF + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $DE \perp AC$ at point F, $\therefore$ $\angle ADE + \angle DAF = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD = \angle EDA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD \sim \triangle EDA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{EA} = \frac{CD}{AD}$,\\
$\therefore$ $EA = \frac{{\left(4\sqrt{2}\right)}^2}{8} = 4$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE = \sqrt{AD^2 + EA^2} = \sqrt{{\left(4\sqrt{2}\right)}^2 + 4^2} = \boxed{4\sqrt{3}}$.

Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rectangle, AD = BC = 4√2, CD = AB = 8, and AD ⟂ AB, AD ⟂ CD. From DE ⟂ AC, it can be known that ∠ADE and ∠DAF are complementary; also, in right triangle ACD, ∠DAF is ∠DAC, so ∠DAC and ∠ACD are complementary. Therefore ∠EDA = ∠ACD. Also ∠DAE = ∠ADC = 90°, so △ACD ∼ △EDA. From the corresponding side relationship of similar triangles, AD/EA = CD/AD, therefore EA = AD²/CD = (4√2)²/8 = 32/8 = 4. Finally, in right triangle ADE, DE = √(AD² + AE²) = √((4√2)² + 4²) = √(32 + 16) = √48 = 4√3.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, $AB=8$, $BC=4\sqrt{2}$, $DE\perp AC$ at point $F$, and intersects $AB$ at point $E$. Find the length of $DE$.
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} In rectangle $ABCD$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAB = \angle ADC = 90^\circ$, $CD = AB = 8$, $AD = BC = 4\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DAF + \angle ACD = 90^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $DE \perp AC$ at point $F$, $\therefore$ $\angle ADE + \angle DAF = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle ACD = \angle EDA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ACD \sim \triangle EDA$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AD}{EA} = \frac{CD}{AD}$,\\
$\therefore$ $EA = \frac{{\left(4\sqrt{2}\right)}^2}{8} = 4$,\\
$\therefore$ $DE = \sqrt{AD^2 + EA^2} = \sqrt{{\left(4\sqrt{2}\right)}^2 + 4^2} = \boxed{4\sqrt{3}}$.
